held_because: real finding not applicable (quote found 0x): while my breast was still near a child being lifted to it
source:
Fragmenta in epistulam ad Romanos
ΑΡΕΘΑ ∆ΙΑΚΟΝΟΥ
Εἰ καί μοι λύχνον αἰῶνος ταχὺς ἔσβεσεν οἶτος λαμπάδος ἡμετέρης φέγγος
ἀμερσάμενος, ἀλλά γ' ἄρ' ἤρκεσε λύσσῃ ἑῆς κακότητος ὁ δαίμων πᾶσαν ἐμὴν τελέσαι
στυγναλέην βιοτήν· θῆκέ με χήρην ἐγγὺς ἀειρομένου μοι μαζοῦ, οὐδ' ἐπὶ τέκνον
ἴδον καλὸν ἀθυρόμενον, ἡδὺ τοκεῦσιν ἄγαλμα παραγκάς· τῷ γέ με πένθος ἄτλητον
μαλερῷ τηκεδόνος δάμασε πυρσῷ· τρεῖς πρὸς ἐείκοσ' ἐποιχομένην ἐνιαυτοὺς ἔσχεν
τύμβος ὅδε ξεινοδόκος γενέθλης ἡμετέρης· ἔνθ' ὕφηνον γενετῆρες ἅπασι γηραλέοι
θρῆνον τιλλόμενοι πολιὴν καὶ χορὸς εὐγενέων στενάχοντες ἀδελφῶν Ἄννης
μνώμενοι ἀσπασίως εἴδεος ἀγλαΐης.
english: Even if swift doom quenched the lamp of my life, robbing our torch of its light, still the demon in the rage of his malice was strong enough to make my whole life gloomy. He made me a widow when my breast had only just begun to rise, and I never saw a lovely child playing, the sweet delight of its parents in their arms. So unbearable grief subdued me with the fierce torch of wasting. This tomb, host to our family, received me as I was passing through my twenty-third year. Here my aged parents wove a lament before everyone, tearing their grey hair, and the chorus of noble brothers groaned, fondly remembering the splendor of Anna's beauty.

findings.quote: while my breast was still near a child being lifted to it
findings.checker_says: Reverses sense: Greek says breast near being lifted (to mouth), not breast near a child being lifted.
findings.reviewer_note: ἐγγὺς ἀειρομένου μαζοῦ = when her breast was just rising (very young); current English invents a nursing child, contradicting the next line (she never saw a child). Quote is stale; fix targets 'He made me a widow while a child was still being lifted to my breast'.

findings.checker_says: πυρσῷ is torch/brand, but τηκεδόνος is wasting/grief; 'firebrand of wasting' is opaque and wrong.
findings.reviewer_note: μαλερῷ τηκεδόνος πυρσῷ = fierce torch of wasting; English is literal and accurate, if stiff.

findings.quote: a sweet delight at parents' knees
findings.checker_says: Misreads παραγκάς (at the elbow/arms, i.e., in parents' embrace), not 'at parents' knees'.
findings.reviewer_note: παραγκάς = in the arms; 'at parents' knees' is an equivalent English image for a small child near its parents.
